author: A Robot
objectives: Students will identify heart anatomy and trace blood flow.
Students will explain structural-functional relationships like wall thickness and valve operation.

modules.description: Orientation of the heart models in anatomical position.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Identify the gross orientation of the heart in anatomical position.
Understand patient-based perspective in anatomical labeling.
instructions: Rotate the models to view the posterior and anterior aspects.

clips.changeMeaning: Spawn the two heart models side by side to establish anatomical orientation for the student.
clips.narration: Welcome. Today we explore the human heart. Observe two models: the intact heart on your left, and a cutaway view on your right. Note that labels are from the patient's perspective, so the right side of the heart is on your left.

clips.changeMeaning: The student is encouraged to rotate the models to see the apex and posterior vessels clearly.
clips.narration: You may rotate these models to examine the apex and major vessel attachments from any angle.

modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Map interior chambers to exterior vessel locations.
instructions: Follow the narration to locate each structure.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlighting the right atrium on the cutaway model to show its superior positioning.
clips.narration: Let us begin our tour with the four chambers. First, the right atrium, the receiving chamber for deoxygenated blood.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlighting the right ventricle, which is the chamber that pumps blood toward the pulmonary circuit.
clips.narration: Next is the right ventricle, which pumps blood to the lungs.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlighting the tricuspid valve, the atrioventricular valve between the right atrium and right ventricle.
clips.narration: Between them sits the tricuspid valve, ensuring one-way flow.
